pageCache.pageTitle: Martock Church School - Vision and Values
pageCache.text:
Vision and Values
Our School vision is at the centre of our decisions for our pupils and staff. It has been agreed by our stakeholders.
'We believe in giving our children and staff the chance to flourish in a nurturing environment with excellent opportunities. We want everyone to experience success and make a positive difference to the world around them.'
Our school bible verse is;
' For I know the plans I have for you, declares the Lord. Plans to prosper you and not harm you, plans to give you a hope and a future.' Jeremiah 29:11
At Martock Church School, we are proud of our Christian Distinctiveness. Everyone is welcome in our school, all faiths, world views or none. We endeavour to live out our school vision so that every child can flourish, with a hope and future. We serve families from our local community, with visits from members of faiths including churches, charities and businesses.
Our vision is at the heart of all we do, our partnerships, our Trust Local Committee, outside agencies and of course, the children.
Our school is an inclusive, welcoming place for children of all backgrounds. As a Church of England school, our values are linked to the Bible.;
Kindness- Linked to the Good Samaritan (Luke 10)
Perserverance - as shown by the friends of the paralysed man (Mark 2)
Respect - as demonstrated in the story of The Roman Centurion ( Matthew 8)
Collaboration - as shown by Noah and his family as they built the ark (Genesis 6-9)
SIAMS
We welcomed the SIAMS inspector to our school on 18th September 2024 to identify how we are upholding our Christian Distinctiveness. We are proud of our report and feedback.
SIAMS
Courageous Advocacy
Part of our vision is that children can make a difference to the world around them. We encourage the children to speak out when the children spot injustice, inequality and for those whose voices are not heard.
At Martock Church School, we believe that we should enable all children to be able to do this, no matter their age or background. We build in opportunities through our Martock Passport, extra oppportunities to celebrate making a difference. Our school council explore opportunities that are close to our hearts, planning carefully a way to make a difference.
Community and Parish Links
Our school is closely linked with All Saints Church in Martock. We have an excellent partnership with the church, attending for special events and services such as Easter, Christmas, RE lessons, spirituality sessions and more. The Open the book team also attend our school to deliver collective worship regularly, which the children love.

Welcome to Martock Church School
Welcome to Martock Church school. We are a friendly, open and supportive school; one who puts our children at the centre of everything we do each day. Our values are Kindness, Perseverance, Collaboration and Respect. We are values-led in all our provision.
We are ambitious about the learning for our children here. Our talented staff team believe in the opportunities and abilities of all children. We have high expectations of behaviour and a nurturing and inclusive heart.
If there is any further information you require, or you have any questions or concerns, do not hesitate to see me, or any member of staff.
Mrs Lafferty-Jenkins

EYFS new Starters
New Starters Reception Class 2026
We look forward to welcoming our newest children to our school on Monday 7th September. Parents should walk their children all the way to the KS1 playground where Mrs Coate will meet the children at the Reception class entrance.
Full time attendance is encouraged though parents have the preference.
Our school gates open at 8.35am
Children need to be in school by 8.45am every morning.
School finishes at 3.15pm every day. The children will leave from the same Reception classroom door.
The Reception learning area is a spacious and engaging place to learn, grow and make friends. We know that children who feel happy, safe and relaxed will thrive in a nurturing environment with the excellent opportunities that we can offer.
If you have any questions or queries, don't hesitate to get in touch with Mrs Loy or Mrs Claringbold on 01935 823486 or email the office [email protected]
Mrs Lafferty-Jenkins

Our Governors
Martock Church School is part of the Bath and Wells Multi Academy Trust.
The school has a Trust Local Committee (TLC).
TLCs are responsible for localised challenge and support on standards, safeguarding, SEND and Stakeholder engagement – the 4S agenda. They also maintain strategic oversight in relation to financial management, health and safety and the school estate. As part of their work, the TLC ensures that Christian distinctiveness permeates all aspects of school life. They are advisory in nature, and their responsibilities are delegated from the Board through the Trust’s Scheme of Delegation. The TLCs also provide local assurance for the board on the experiences of pupils, parents/carers, staff and the wider community.
The TLC meets six times per year supported by a Governance Professional. The Governance Professional at Martock Church School is Mrs Jill Webb.
The Board of Trustees can delegate some its responsibilities to other layers of the governance structure. This is done through the Scheme of Delegation. You can find out more about the Trust's Scheme of Delegation here Bath and Wells Multi Academy Trust - Scheme of Delegation.
If you would like to contact the Chair of Governors, please contact the school office.

Attendance
At Martock Church School, we know that good attendance enables pupils to make good friendships, secure learning and develop resilience. We know that good attendance has a direct link to future prospects for learning and later life. We encourage all children to aim for a high level of attendance (97%) to meet with these expectations. National expectations are at 96%. This is the same as 177 days out of a possible 190 days. Attendance which is regular and on time is important for all children to succeed. We want to work with parents to ensure that children have a personalised approach to managing attendance, which includes support and guidance, where needed.
The School Day
The school day starts at 8.45am. Morning registration starts at 8.45am. Gates are open to families from 8.35am and close at 8.45am. Children can enter their classrooms straight away.
We have two ten minutes breaks during the morning and one lunch break time. The afternoons may incorporate outdoor learning and breaks.
Lunch times- Lunch time runs from 12pm- 1pm every day.
End of the school day- School ends at 3.15pm for all children. Parents are encouraged to collect their youngest child first.
Total hours in a typical week- the total hours are 32.5 hours each week.
Recording attendance.
Each 1/2 a day at school has to be recorded as either authorised or unauthorised.
Authorised absences- illness, medical appointment, emergencies.
Unauthorised absences
We are guided by the DFE to record all absences. Please see our attendance policy.
Examples of unauthorised absences
Letting us know if your child is absent
If your child is unwell, please call the office on 01935 823486 and leave a message by selection option Alternatively, you can email the office using the email address: [email protected]
If we haven't heard from you and your child does not arrive into school, we will contact you initially by text and will follow this up with a telephone call. It's important that we establish where your child is to ensure that they are safe. If we have concerns that we have not heard from you, we may carry out a home visit.
Punctuality is very important. Lateness results in children not feeling ready to learn, missing out on activities as well as lost learning. This all adds up over time. We know that children who regularly arrive late do not succeed as well as other children do. Please make every effort to arrive early to allow your child to be ready to start learning at 8.45am.
Please be aware that time off school for a holiday usually incurs a fixed penalty for both parents, unless it is an exceptional circumstance (funeral, wedding etc). Decisions are made by the school though this is a County procedure. Governors have agreed to this procedure. Even if your holiday includes educational visits, we won't be able to authorise it.

Curriculum
Curriculum areas
Welcome to our curriculum page. Click on the links below to explore each subject and learn more about what is taught across our school.
Art and Design PSHE and RSHE English
Religious Education Maths PE- Physical Education
History Phonics and Early Reading
At Martock Church School, we want our pupils to experience success through an exciting and cohesive curriculum. Our curriculum aims to provide engaging opportunities both in and out of school. The curriculum is organised so that children know more and remember more, through building blocks of knowledge and skills.
Where appropriate, we ensure that cross curricular links are made (e.g. within topics) to enhance learning and make it relevant to children's interest and experiences. We ensure the children have a range of learning experiences that challenge, stimulate and promote thinking and learning. The curriculum, including core skills in Literacy and Numeracy, meets all statutory requirements. It is designed to enthuse our children with a love of learning.
We strive to provide a curriculum which has a variety of enrichment activities that are integrated into the curriculum plans for each year group throughout the school year, both in and out of the classroom environment.
We are will aware that all children need the support of parents and teachers to make good progress in school. We build positive links with the parents and carers of each child, by regularly keeping them informed about the way in which the children are being taught and how well each child is progressing.
Please see our Curriculum Policy.
Opting out of Religious Education
At Martock Church School, we believe in fostering an inclusive environment where every child's beliefs and values are respected. We understand that some parents may wish to withdraw their child from Religious Education (RE) lessons. If you would like to opt your child out of the RE curriculum, please contact the school office on 01935 823486, and we will provide further guidance on how to proceed.
If you have any questions or concerns, feel free to reach out to your class teacher or Mrs Lafferty-Jenkins for more information.

Remote Learning
When we aren't able to offer face to face teaching, we offer remote learning through our Google Classrooms platform. Each child has their own unique login to access learning materials. We will also choose to add links to our class pages for additional information.
Children who are unable to attend school for medical reasons may be offered alternative provision. Please see our supporting medical needs policy.

pageCache.pageTitle: Martock Church School - Coral Class- Reception
pageCache.text:
Coral Class- Reception
Welcome to Coral Class, where every child is encouraged to feel happy, safe and valued from the moment they walk through the door. We are a friendly, caring and nurturing class where kindness, respect and positive relationships are at the heart of everything we do. Through a balance of play-based experiences and purposeful teaching, we inspire children to develop a love of learning while building confidence, independence and curiosity.
Our exciting and engaging learning environment provides opportunities for children to explore, discover and develop new skills both indoors and outdoors. We celebrate each child's unique strengths and interests, encouraging them to take risks, ask questions and persevere when faced with challenges. Through stories, creative activities, practical experiences and collaborative play, children develop important early skills in communication, literacy, mathematics and personal development.
We work closely with parents and carers, recognising the importance of partnership in supporting every child's learning journey. Together, we create a warm, welcoming community where children have fun, make friends and thrive as they take their first steps through school.
Mrs Coate - Class Teacher
